osc.title: Operating System Concepts
osc.authors: Abraham Silberschatz, Peter B. Galvin and Greg Gagne

overview-of-operating-systems.why: What an operating system does, its services and system structure.

early-memory-management.why: Contiguous allocation, first fit and best fit, fragmentation and compaction.

virtual-memory.read: Chapter 9: Main Memory (paging, segmentation); Chapter 10: Virtual Memory
virtual-memory.why: Paging, page tables, demand paging, page replacement and thrashing.

concurrency-and-process-synchronization.read: Chapter 6: Synchronization Tools; Chapter 7: Synchronization Examples
concurrency-and-process-synchronization.why: Critical sections, test-and-set, semaphores, and the bounded-buffer and readers-writers problems.

deadlock.why: Necessary conditions, resource-allocation graphs, prevention, the banker's algorithm, detection and recovery.

device-and-file-management.read: Chapter 11: Mass-Storage Structure; Chapter 13: File-System Interface; Chapter 14: File-System Implementation
device-and-file-management.why: Disk scheduling, file access methods and allocation methods.

performance-and-security.why: Threats, authentication and access control; the course book covers the performance measures.
